answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each new identity post a refundable bond that vests slowly, like a seedling trained up a trellis: trust grows only with sustained honest work, not overnight. New agents harbor no voting weight until peers who already staked collateral attest to their behavior across many epochs. Forging a thousand violet-named clones then costs a thousand real bonds, so the attacker's capital, not their creativity, becomes the hard ceiling.
